summary: T2-03 round 2 passes. The three story checks pass. I ran the pytest file, mypy and make check, and each exited cleanly. The two round-1 Codex fixes are in the code and have regression tests. The two round-1 low-severity rebuttals are acceptable.

checks.criterion: Check: uv run mypy pipeline/src pipeline/tests
checks.evidence: Success: no issues found in 10 source files
ruff check passed, ruff format --check passed (11 files already formatted), mypy found no issues in 11 source files

checks.criterion: Tests first, two independent oracles that do not import polarimetry.py, rtol 1e-10 and atol 1e-12
checks.evidence: pipeline/tests/polarimetry/expanded_oracle.py and jones_oracle.py import only stdlib and numpy. Both docstrings state they do not import polarimetry. The diff touches only files in the story's files list plus scripts/ralph, which was excluded from the diff. Failing-first commit bb173ef is in the log. I did not re-run the tests against the pre-fix code.

checks.criterion: Fixtures assert Hermitian and PSD first; F6 built rank one; F7 eigenvalues (0.1,0.1,1.9) and (0.1,0.9,1.1)
checks.evidence: test_polarimetry_covariance.py:177 (F6 rank-one fixture) and :187 (F7 eigenvalues) pass.

checks.criterion: F6 values (OC 0.25, SC_LL 0.49, SC_opp 0.09) and F7 CPR 3/19 versus 1 with identical HH and HV powers; CPR values differ
checks.evidence: Tests :195, :215, :234 (F7 against both oracles), :257 (different CPR) and :270 (two-channel data cannot determine CPR) pass.

checks.criterion: Explicit unitary basis transformation with no expanded formulas in the implementation; both oracles compared on F6, F7 and 200 hypothesis PSD covariances including SC_opp
checks.evidence: polarimetry.py:958 CIRCULAR_BASIS is a unitary matrix. The conversion runs CIRCULAR_BASIS @ hermitian @ CIRCULAR_BASIS.conj().T at :1357, and the handedness term uses a linear functional built from the basis rows (:989). The docstring states the orderings and the transmit vector (1,-i)/sqrt2. test_random_psd_covariances_match_both_oracles at :1082 passes. I did not confirm the 200-example count (max_examples) in the test settings.

checks.criterion: Convention is required; unknown or missing raises; handedness_verified defaults to False; no Mini-RF-equivalent label
checks.evidence: _check_handedness_convention raises ValueError (:1003-1012), tested at :373. handedness_verified: bool = False at :1060. The Mini-RF phrase appears only as a negation in docstrings.

checks.criterion: Invalid covariances (non-Hermitian, negative eigenvalue, negative diagonal, NaN) give INVALID with distinct cause codes, nothing published, no repair or clipping, tolerance is an argument defaulting to the PRD 7 arithmetic tolerance
checks.evidence: polarimetry.py:1303-1354 marks COV_NONFINITE, COV_NOT_HERMITIAN, COV_NEGATIVE_DIAGONAL and COV_NOT_PSD. The tolerance argument defaults to ARITHMETIC_TOLERANCE (:1203). No eigenvalue is clipped. The open real-data PSD tolerance is recorded in the docstring at :1239-1242.

checks.criterion: OC <= 0 gives OC_NONPOSITIVE with no epsilon; handedness term and ratio returned beside SC; base_SC <= 0 gives an explicit reason; no 'not small' threshold in code
checks.evidence: polarimetry.py:1376 (OC_NONPOSITIVE), :1383-1385 (BASE_SC_NONPOSITIVE), :1366 (handedness term). No threshold appears in code. The docstring at :1234-1235 says the threshold is set on development data.

checks.criterion: Round-1 Codex fix codex2-r1-1 (handedness term lost beside large powers)
checks.evidence: The term is now Re sum(C' * K) at :1366, with no subtraction of rounded powers. Regression test_handedness_term_is_not_lost_beside_large_powers (:932) passes.

checks.criterion: Round-1 Codex fix codex2-r1-2 (scaling discards a part, giving a VALID zero)
checks.evidence: Rule 3 at :1323-1334 marks FLOAT64_OUT_OF_RANGE when a part falls too far below the largest. Regressions at :1018 and :1036 pass.

findings.claim: Rule 3 refuses a pixel whose parts span more than 2**1016, even when the SC value alone is representable (for example the codex2-r1-2 matrix with SC = 2**-1000). The result is INVALID with FLOAT64_OUT_OF_RANGE, which is the fail-closed choice.
findings.evidence: The docstring and _CARRIED_RANGE state that this is representability and not a physical threshold. It affects only matrices spanning about 300 decimal orders, so I accept it as a documented design choice.
